title: The private space race is spurring a luxury hotel land grab for Florida oceanfront property
raw_text:
Key Points
- The rise of the private space industry, with companies like SpaceX and Blue Origin, has spurred demand for commercial real estate on Florida's space coast.
- A new $420 million Westin Cocoa Beach Resort & Spa is set to open next year complete with a conference center.
- Once the Westin opens, Miami-based Driftwood Capital will control about 62% of the beachfront hotel inventory in the region, according to executive chairman Carlos Rodriguez Sr.
